_disclaimer: These are general, commonly used active-ingredient groups and bio-agents, not a prescription, and no doses are given. Registered products and rules vary by crop and state, so always get written guidance from your local agricultural officer or Krishi Vigyan Kendra before buying or applying anything. Listed stores are examples, not endorsements, and you should buy only from licensed sellers. Wrong products or wrong use can harm crops, people, and the environment.

recommended_products: Contact protectant fungicide (e.g., captan or mancozeb)
Apple___Apple_scab.note: Rake up and destroy fallen leaves, and prune the canopy for better airflow.

Apple___Black_rot.note: Prune out dead wood and cankers, and remove mummified fruit before any spraying.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.note: Remove nearby juniper or red cedar trees where practical, since the disease needs both hosts.

recommended_products: Compost or vermicompost to support tree health
Apple___healthy.note: Keep the canopy pruned for airflow and inspect leaves and fruit regularly.

recommended_products: Organic mulch to help keep the soil acidic
Soil-test-based nutrition only if a test shows a need
Blueberry___healthy.note: Use drip irrigation and avoid wetting the leaves.

recommended_products: Triazole-group fungicide (only on agricultural officer's advice)
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.note: Act at the first signs, and avoid sulphur sprays in very hot weather because they can burn leaves.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.note: Prune for airflow and remove fallen leaves and fruit.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.note: Check lower leaves regularly, rotate with non-cereal crops, and bury or remove crop residue after harvest.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.note: Use resistant hybrids, and monitor fields in cool, damp weather. Treat only if the infection is spreading.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.note: Bury or remove infected crop residue and avoid growing maize on the same field year after year.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.note: Keep scouting the field and maintain recommended plant spacing.

recommended_products: Systemic triazole fungicide (only on agricultural officer's advice)
Grape___Black_rot.note: Remove all mummified berries from the vines and the ground, and keep the canopy open.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).note: Avoid large pruning wounds in wet weather, disinfect pruning tools between vines, and remove severely affected vines.

recommended_products: Copper-based spray (e.g., copper oxychloride or Bordeaux mixture)
Systemic fungicide (only on agricultural officer's advice)
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.note: Remove fallen infected leaves and keep the canopy open for airflow.

recommended_products: Canopy management for sunlight and airflow
Organic soil enrichers such as farmyard manure
Grape___healthy.note: Maintain trellis training and balanced feeding.

recommended_products: No curative chemical is available for this bacterial disease
Insect control for the Asian citrus psyllid, using only products approved by your agricultural officer
Neem-based formulation to help deter the psyllid
Zinc and iron micronutrient spray to ease deficiency symptoms (this does not cure the disease)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).note: Remove severely infected trees, plant only certified disease-free material, and report suspected cases to the agriculture department.

recommended_products: Other bactericide only where registered for this crop and prescribed by an agricultural officer
Peach___Bacterial_spot.note: Apply copper only at the stages your officer or the product label advises, because it can harm leaves and fruit at the wrong time.

recommended_products: Orchard hygiene, such as removing fallen leaves and fruit
Peach___healthy.note: Avoid too much nitrogen, which causes soft growth that diseases favour.

recommended_products: Other bactericide only where registered for this crop and prescribed by an agricultural officer
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.note: Use disease-free seed or seedlings, avoid overhead watering, and avoid working in wet fields.

recommended_products: Neem cake as a soil amendment
Pepper,_bell___healthy.note: Use drip irrigation and check the undersides of leaves from time to time.

recommended_products: Protective contact fungicide (e.g., mancozeb or chlorothalonil)
Potato___Early_blight.note: Start protection when lower leaves show ringed spots, and keep plant nutrition balanced.

recommended_products: Systemic and contact combination (e.g., metalaxyl with mancozeb, or cymoxanil with mancozeb)
Potato___Late_blight.note: Late blight spreads very fast in cool, wet, foggy weather. Contact your agricultural officer immediately and destroy infected plants and discarded tubers.

recommended_products: Earthing up soil around the plants
Potato___healthy.note: Keep scouting, especially in cool, humid weather.

recommended_products: Compost and cane support or trellising
Watering at the base of the plant
Raspberry___healthy.note: Prune out old fruited canes after harvest.

recommended_products: Rhizobium seed inoculation for the next crop
Soybean___healthy.note: Keep the crop weed-free and keep scouting.

recommended_products: Systemic triazole fungicide (only on agricultural officer's advice)
Squash___Powdery_mildew.note: Spray in the early morning or evening and cover the undersides of the leaves.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.note: Remove and destroy badly spotted leaves, grow on raised beds with clean mulch, and give plants room.

recommended_products: Clean straw mulch to keep fruit off the soil
Strawberry___healthy.note: Check crowns and runners regularly for spots.

recommended_products: Bio-control agent (Bacillus subtilis or Pseudomonas fluorescens)
Other bactericide only where registered for this crop and prescribed by an agricultural officer
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.note: Use disease-free seed and healthy seedlings, and avoid working among wet plants.

Tomato___Early_blight.note: Remove lower leaves that touch the soil, and mulch to stop rain splashing spores upward.

recommended_products: Preventive multi-site fungicide (e.g., mancozeb or chlorothalonil)
Systemic and contact combination (e.g., metalaxyl-M with mancozeb, or cymoxanil with mancozeb)
Tomato___Late_blight.note: Late blight can ruin a crop within days in cool, wet weather. Isolate infected plants and contact your agricultural officer immediately.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.note: Mostly a problem in polyhouses and greenhouses: reduce humidity and improve ventilation.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.note: Remove infected lower leaves quickly, avoid overhead watering, and rotate with non-tomato-family crops.

recommended_products: Acaricide (miticide) registered for this crop, only on agricultural officer's advice
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.note: Mites thrive in hot, dry, dusty conditions. Spray the undersides of leaves well, keep plants watered, and rotate between chemical groups if sprays are needed.

Tomato___Target_Spot.note: Give plants room and stake them for airflow, and clean supports between seasons.

recommended_products: No curative chemical is available for virus infections
Yellow sticky traps to monitor and reduce whiteflies
Neem-based formulation as a whitefly deterrent
Systemic insecticide only on agricultural officer's advice
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.note: Remove and destroy infected plants early, and use insect-proof nets in nurseries.

recommended_products: No chemical cure is available for plant viruses
Disinfect hands and tools between plants (method as advised by your agricultural officer)
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.note: The virus spreads by touch and tools. Do not handle tobacco before touching plants, and remove infected plants.

recommended_products: Beneficial soil microbes (e.g., Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) for soil health
Tomato___healthy.note: Keep staking, pruning suckers, and watering at the base of the plant.
